verdict.summary: Yatharth Hospitality (53/100) — Reject/AVOID. RS percentile of only 37 fails Trend Template criterion c8 (needs ≥70), the sole gate failure but a hard one per Prime Directive 4: no scoring override permits an actionable buy while Trend Template is unconfirmed. Fundamentally the story is decent but decelerating — strong sales growth (21-47% YoY) and margin durability questions (net margin down 365bps YoY, OPM slipping from 25% to 23%), rising other-income contribution to PBT (13-16% range, approaching the 30% red-flag threshold but not breaching it), soft ROE/ROCE (10.4%/12.4%, both below Minervini quality thresholds), zero institutional sponsorship score, and no group leadership (ranked 6 of 6 in its industry group). Price is technically tight — inside a 2nd base, 11 weeks, 12.8% deep, sitting just 2.2% below the 52-week high and 2.18% under a 889.9 pivot — but RS strength has not confirmed the pattern. This is a name to watch for an RS re-acceleration into the 70s, not to buy.
strengths: Revenue growth strong and accelerating (B1=6, B2=4): 21-47% YoY over last 4 quarters
Clean balance sheet: D/E 0.15, interest coverage 41.7x, zero pledge
Tight, orderly base structure forming just under the 52-week high (2.2% below), 2nd base since Stage 2
Top-quartile industry group RS (H1=2) despite weak intra-group rank
weaknesses: RS percentile only 37 — fails Gate 1 criterion c8, the binding constraint on the whole setup
Net margin contracting YoY (-365bps) and OPM trending down (25%→23%) despite revenue growth
Weakest company in its own industry group by leadership rank (6 of 6)
ROE (10.4%) and ROCE (12.4%) below Minervini quality bar
EPS acceleration inconsistent (A2=1) despite decent annual growth
5 fields unverified (FCF, governance events, marquee institution, MF scheme count, new catalyst) — each scored 0 per Prime Directive 2
verdict.biggest_risk: Relative strength failure (RS=37) signals the stock is not being accumulated by institutions relative to the broader market — until this reverses, any base breakout lacks the market-leadership confirmation Minervini requires, risking a low-follow-through or failed breakout even if price clears the 889.9 pivot.
